searchText: <nibnalin> It looks like the recommended address for the P256VERIFY precompile is different between EIP-7212 and RIP-7212 -- I think it would be better to redirect both proposals to the same page to avoid confusion, not sure who runs the website -- https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7212 cc @adietrichs <nibnalin> ^cc @adietrichs <SamWilsn> I do <SamWilsn> I'm not entirely sure what to do with 7212 <SamWilsn> Would make the most sense to integrate rendering the two sites, but I'm not sure what the plan is overall. <nibnalin> Makes sense, the most immediate thing is that PRECOMPILED_ADDRESS in the EIP is not the same as the RIP, and I can imagine this causing confusion, should I make a PR to make them the same? <SamWilsn> That'd be up to the authors of it EIP7212 was meant to be removed, as it was moved from an EIP to a RIP. Otherwise RIP would have been issued a new number. As per the discussion in the PR: https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/pull/5#pullrequestreview-1789799774 <ulerdogan> I think the plan should be removing EIP-7212 as it migrated to an RIP and there is kind of conflict by numbers. There is an open PR for that, but have blockers: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/8101 (re @nibnalin: Makes sense, the most immediate thing is that PRECOMPILED_ADDRESS in the EIP is not the same as the RIP, and I can imagine this causing confusion, should I make a PR to make them the same?) <dcposch> I don't quite understand why the RIP returns empty data instead of 0 / 1 now. https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/pull/19/files#r1602718444 In that case, how does a contract tell whether the precompile exists? <drortirosh> Is there an rips site yet? Last time I checked, there isn't even a DNS entry for rips.ethereum.org (re @SamWilsn: Would make the most sense to integrate rendering the two sites, but I'm not sure what the plan is overall.) <CarlBeek> There is not, need to do a bunch of work to make RIPs into a site, even ercs.ethereum.org doesn't really work. since the EIPs/ERCs split the site(s) need some work (re @drortirosh: Is there an rips site yet? Last time I checked, there isn't even a DNS entry for rips.ethereum.org) <ulerdogan> The spec has not changed, just changed to address misunderstandings. It's aligned with chain implementation. (re @dcposch: I don't quite understand why the RIP returns empty data instead of 0 / 1 now. https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/pull/19/files#r1602718444 In that case, how does a contract tell whether the precompile exists?) <ulerdogan> Is this work not enough to render? https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/pull/17 (re @CarlBeek: There is not, need to do a bunch of work to make RIPs into a site, even ercs.ethereum.org doesn't really work. since the EIPs/ERCs split the site(s) need some work) <CarlBeek> i’ll dm not to blow up this channel (re @ulerdogan: Is this work not enough to render? https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/pull/17)

excerpts.content:

excerpts.author: abcoathup
excerpts.content:
EIP7212 was meant to be removed, as it was moved from an EIP to a RIP.  Otherwise RIP would have been issued a new number.  
As per the discussion in the PR:
https://github.com/ethereum/RIPs/pull/5#pullrequestreview-1789799774

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <ulerdogan> I think the plan should be removing EIP-7212 as it migrated to an RIP and there is kind of conflict by numbers.
